speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. To help me understand what's going on, can you tell me if you’ve had any recent headaches, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light? Also, have you noticed any rashes or changes in your vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current haloperidol use, have you experienced any muscle stiffness, rigidity, or excessive sweating? I need to determine if this could be Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome rather than an infectious process.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

Do you have any history of recent infection or exposure to other antipsychotic medications?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The markedly elevated creatine kinase, combined with fever, rigidity, and altered mentation in the context of haloperidol use, strongly points to Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I have sufficient information to confirm the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
